questions.question_text: Read the provided unseen passage tracking modern digital work habits. According to the author, what is the primary cause of 'digital burnout' among remote employees?
options: A) Lack of high-speed internet connectivity
B) The complete absence of physical office spaces
C) The blurring of boundaries between professional hours and personal time
D) Insufficient technical training on software platforms
questions.answer: C) The blurring of boundaries between professional hours and personal time

questions.question_text: Based on the passage, the phrase 'always-on culture' refers to:
options: A) Keeping computer monitors switched on 24/7 to save reboot time
B) The societal expectation that employees must be continuously available and responsive to digital communications
C) A new corporate policy enforcing uninterrupted streaming of company meetings
D) The reliable power grid infrastructure supporting modern cities
questions.answer: B) The societal expectation that employees must be continuously available and responsive to digital communications

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank based on the text: The author suggests that implementing a strict 'right to ___________' policy could significantly improve employee mental health.
options: A) travel
B) disconnect
C) complain
D) negotiate
questions.answer: B) disconnect

questions.question_text: How does the passage distinguish between 'productivity' and 'presence' in a remote work environment? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The passage argues that 'presence' merely involves being online and visible on communication tools, whereas 'productivity' is the actual completion of meaningful tasks. It stresses that being constantly online does not automatically translate to efficient or quality output.

questions.question_text: What two strategies does the author recommend for managers to help their teams avoid digital fatigue? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Managers should establish clear communication boundaries by prohibiting non-urgent emails after work hours. Furthermore, they should encourage asynchronous communication, allowing employees to respond to messages at their own pace rather than expecting immediate replies.

questions.question_text: Analyze why the author believes that 'digital detox' weekends are a flawed solution to chronic overwork. [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The author considers 'digital detox' weekends a flawed solution because they only treat the symptoms temporarily. They fail to address the root cause, which is a toxic daily work culture that demands constant connectivity during the week.

sections.section_name: Section B - Writing Skills & Applied Grammar

questions.question_text: Identify the option that correctly converts the given direct dialog into Reported Speech: The teacher said to the students, "Do not submit your assignments late."
options: A) The teacher said to the students to not submit their assignments late.
B) The teacher ordered the students not to submit their assignments late.
C) The teacher asked the students if they will submit their assignments late.
D) The teacher commanded the students do not submit their assignments late.
questions.answer: B) The teacher ordered the students not to submit their assignments late.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the most appropriate determiner: We have to hurry. We don't have ___________ time left before the train departs.
options: A) many
B) some
C) much
D) few
questions.answer: C) much

questions.question_text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence showcasing proper subject-verb concord:
options: A) The committee of experts are divided on the new policy.
B) Neither the manager nor the employees was aware of the meeting.
C) Every student and every teacher were present at the assembly.
D) Bread and butter is his favorite breakfast.
questions.answer: D) Bread and butter is his favorite breakfast.

questions.question_text: Identify the error and supply the correction for the following sentence: 'The museum have a remarkable collection of ancient artifacts.'
options: A) Error: remarkable, Correction: remarking
B) Error: ancient, Correction: old
C) Error: have, Correction: has
D) Error: of, Correction: for
questions.answer: C) Error: have, Correction: has

questions.question_text: Select the correct Reported Speech for the question: 'She asked him, "Where are you planning to go for the summer holidays?"'
options: A) She asked him where was he planning to go for the summer holidays.
B) She asked him where he is planning to go for the summer holidays.
C) She asked him where he was planning to go for the summer holidays.
D) She asked him where you are planning to go for the summer holidays.
questions.answer: C) She asked him where he was planning to go for the summer holidays.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the correct modal verb to indicate a strong moral obligation: As citizens, we ________ respect the fundamental rights of others.
options: A) might
B) ought to
C) could
D) would
questions.answer: B) ought to

questions.question_text: Identify the option that correctly converts the given direct dialog into Reported Speech: "I have finished the report," Sarah said.
options: A) Sarah said that she had finished the report.
B) Sarah said that I have finished the report.
C) Sarah said that she has finished the report.
D) Sarah says that she had finished the report.
questions.answer: A) Sarah said that she had finished the report.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank with the appropriate determiner: Is there ________ milk left in the refrigerator for the coffee?
options: A) any
B) few
C) many
D) entirely
questions.answer: A) any

questions.question_text: You ordered a set of encyclopedia volumes online, but received damaged books. Write a formal letter of complaint to the Customer Service Manager of the publishing company, requesting an immediate replacement or refund. [100-120 words]
questions.answer: Sir, I am writing to register a strong complaint regarding order #8765 placed on your website on 4th October. I ordered the complete 10-volume 'Global Encyclopedia' set. However, upon delivery yesterday, I discovered that volumes 3, 5, and 8 have severely damaged bindings and torn pages, rendering them unusable. This suggests poor packaging and mishandling during transit. As a regular customer, I expect better quality control from your reputed publishing house. I request you to arrange an immediate pickup of the damaged set and either provide a full replacement in pristine condition or process a complete refund to my original payment method at the earliest. Yours faithfully, Rohan Sharma.

questions.question_text: Write an analytical paragraph summarizing the data provided in a pie chart showing the preferred modes of digital entertainment among teenagers (Video Games: 45%, Social Media: 30%, Streaming Movies: 15%, E-books: 10%). [100-120 words]
questions.answer: The given pie chart visually illustrates the varying preferences of teenagers regarding digital entertainment formats. It is strikingly evident that interactive media dominates their leisure time, with video games capturing the largest segment at 45%. This is closely followed by social media engagement, which accounts for 30% of their digital consumption. Together, these two highly interactive and socially connected platforms constitute three-quarters of teenage digital entertainment. In contrast, more passive forms of entertainment show significantly lower engagement. Streaming movies and shows appeal to a moderate 15% of the demographic. The most traditional form of digital consumption, e-books, represents the smallest fraction at a mere 10%. Overall, the data clearly indicates a strong generational shift towards interactive and socially integrated digital activities over passive reading or viewing habits.

questions.question_text: Read the extract from 'Madam Rides the Bus'. What was Valli's strongest, most overwhelming desire?
options: A) To buy new toys from the town fair
B) To ride the bus that traveled between her village and the nearest town
C) To make friends with the village children playing in the street
D) To travel by train across the country
questions.answer: B) To ride the bus that traveled between her village and the nearest town

questions.question_text: From the play 'The Proposal', what is the immediate physical reaction Lomov experiences when he gets overly excited or anxious?
options: A) He starts laughing uncontrollably
B) He faints and loses consciousness immediately
C) He suffers from severe palpitations and twitching
D) He loses his voice and cannot speak
questions.answer: C) He suffers from severe palpitations and twitching

questions.question_text: In 'The Necklace', how does Madame Loisel's fatal flaw of vanity lead to her ultimate ruin? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: Madame Loisel's intense vanity and dissatisfaction with her modest life drive her to borrow a diamond necklace to appear wealthy at a ball. Losing it forces her into a decade of gruelling poverty, completely destroying her youth and beauty, ultimately ruining her life.

questions.question_text: Explain the significance of the title 'The Book That Saved the Earth'. How did an ordinary nursery rhyme book avert a Martian invasion? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: The title is literal. Think-Tank, the Martian ruler, misinterprets the nursery rhymes in 'Mother Goose' as evidence of advanced Earthling technology and aggressive military strategy. Terrified by tales of exploding cows and space-traveling dogs, he cancels the invasion and orders a retreat.

questions.question_text: In 'Bholi', how does the teacher's attitude contrast with Bholi's family's treatment of her, and what impact does this have? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: While Bholi's family neglects and mocks her for her looks and stutter, the teacher treats her with profound affection, patience, and respect. This compassionate support builds Bholi's self-confidence, transforming her from a frightened, stuttering girl into a bold, articulate, and independent young woman.

questions.question_text: What profound realization does Kisa Gotami achieve regarding human mortality in 'The Sermon at Benares'? [30-40 words]
questions.answer: After failing to find a house untouched by death, Kisa Gotami realizes that death is inevitable and common to all. She understands that her immense grief was selfish, and that accepting mortality is the only path to achieving inner peace and overcoming sorrow.

questions.question_text: Analyze the character evolution of Richard Ebright in 'The Making of a Scientist'. How did early failures shape his scientific methodology and drive his eventual success? [100-120 words]
questions.answer: Richard Ebright's journey highlights that genuine scientific achievement stems from perseverance and rigorous experimentation, not merely displaying facts. Initially, at the county science fair, he simply displayed frog tissues under a microscope and lost. This early failure was a pivotal awakening; he realized that winners conducted real, active experiments. Instead of losing hope, he channeled his competitive spirit into rigorous research, seeking guidance from Dr. Urquhart. He began complex, systematic experiments on monarch butterflies, testing hypotheses about viral diseases and viceroy mimicry. His ability to learn from failure, coupled with his innate curiosity, meticulous observation skills, and relentless drive, transformed his methodology. It shifted him from a mere collector of specimens to a pioneering researcher discovering the chemical structure of insect hormones.

questions.question_text: Discuss the central theme of appearances versus reality in 'The Midnight Visitor'. How does Ausable use his intellect and the physical setting to outwit Max? [100-120 words]
questions.answer: The central theme of 'The Midnight Visitor' is that appearances are profoundly deceptive; true capability lies in intellect and presence of mind, not physical stereotypes. Ausable, a fat and sluggish secret agent, looks nothing like the romanticized spies of fiction. However, when confronted by the armed and dangerous Max, Ausable does not panic. Instead, he uses his sharp intellect and quick thinking to weaponize the physical setting of his ordinary hotel room. He fabricates a highly convincing story about a non-existent balcony right outside his window, complaining about it so naturally that Max believes him. When the waiter knocks, Ausable smoothly claims it is the police. Panicked, Max jumps onto the 'balcony' to hide, falling to his death, proving that Ausable's brilliant psychological manipulation completely neutralized a deadly physical threat.
